title: Every British Aircraft Carrier Class Ever Built (2026)

warnings: An 'ever built' title cannot include machines that were not actually built: Illustrious class, Audacious class, Centaur class. Exclude cancelled, merely planned, on-order, and unfinished entries; split mixed class ranges so only completed or launched machines remain.
hard_warnings: An 'ever built' title cannot include machines that were not actually built: Illustrious class, Audacious class, Centaur class. Exclude cancelled, merely planned, on-order, and unfinished entries; split mixed class ranges so only completed or launched machines remain.

roster_pacing_targets.heuristic_note: Runtime target for the locked final roster; research a small reserve for exclusions/swaps, not an endless universe.

unit_roster.name: HMS Argus
unit_roster.role: First British aircraft carrier with full-length flush flight deck, converted liner
unit_roster.built_count: 1 ship completed and commissioned, converted from Italian liner Conte Rosso [IWM 2024]

unit_roster.name: HMS Furious
unit_roster.role: Battlecruiser converted to aircraft carrier, first of Courageous-class conversions
unit_roster.years: Initially converted 1917, fully reconstructed 1921-1925, served until 1945 [Naval Encyclopedia 2024]
unit_roster.built_count: 1 ship completed, converted battlecruiser, reconstructed with full-length flight deck 1921-1925 [Naval Encyclopedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: HMS Hermes (1924)
unit_roster.role: First purpose-designed aircraft carrier, laid down as carrier from keel
unit_roster.years: Laid down January 1918, commissioned February 1924, sunk April 1942 [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: HMS Eagle (1918)
unit_roster.built_count: 1 ship completed, converted from Chilean battleship Almirante Cochrane [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Courageous class
unit_roster.role: Battlecruiser conversions to fleet carriers, Washington Treaty conversions
unit_roster.built_count: 2 ships completed as carriers: HMS Courageous and HMS Glorious, converted 1924-1928 and 1924-1930 respectively [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Ark Royal (1938)
unit_roster.role: First modern purpose-designed fleet carrier, interwar flagship design

unit_roster.name: Illustrious class
unit_roster.role: Armoured fleet carriers, first armoured carriers in the world

unit_roster.name: Implacable class
unit_roster.role: Modified Illustrious design with two-level hangars, faster armoured carriers
unit_roster.years: Commissioned 1944 (Indefatigable May, Implacable August), in service 1944-1955 [Wikipedia 2024]
unit_roster.built_count: 2 ships completed: HMS Implacable and HMS Indefatigable [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: HMS Unicorn
unit_roster.role: Aircraft maintenance carrier, unique support vessel with flight deck
unit_roster.built_count: 1 ship completed, designed as aircraft repair ship and light carrier [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Colossus class
unit_roster.role: Light fleet carriers, 1942 design for rapid wartime construction
unit_roster.built_count: 8 ships completed as aircraft carriers for Royal Navy, plus 2 completed as maintenance carriers (Pioneer, Perseus) [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Majestic class
unit_roster.role: Modified 1942 design light fleet carriers for larger aircraft
unit_roster.years: Built 1943-1961, construction suspended 1945, completed postwar for foreign navies [Wikipedia 2024]
unit_roster.built_count: 5 ships completed (6th, Leviathan, cancelled incomplete), none served in Royal Navy, all sold to foreign navies [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Audacious class
unit_roster.role: Large fleet carriers, postwar completion of wartime design
unit_roster.built_count: 2 ships completed out of 4 planned: HMS Eagle (ex-Audacious) and HMS Ark Royal [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Centaur class
unit_roster.role: Light fleet carriers, final evolution of 1942 design with jet capability
unit_roster.built_count: 4 ships completed out of 8 planned: HMS Centaur, Albion, Bulwark, Hermes [Wikipedia 2024]

unit_roster.name: Invincible class
unit_roster.role: Light VSTOL carriers, through-deck cruisers, Sea Harrier platforms

unit_roster.name: Queen Elizabeth class
unit_roster.role: Current supercarriers, largest Royal Navy ships ever built, F-35B platforms
unit_roster.years: Commissioned 2017 (Queen Elizabeth) and 2019 (Prince of Wales), both currently in service 2026 [Royal Navy 2024]
unit_roster.built_count: 2 ships completed and in service [Royal Navy 2024]
